messages:
jordan_support: Customer (finance corp) opened a case — their Private/VPC deployment is returning TLS handshake failures when clients are behind their corporate HTTP proxy. They only see errors for our inference endpoints over port 443.

samir_neteng: Can you paste a short repro and any error logs? Most enterprise proxies either allow raw CONNECT or terminate TLS. If they terminate, SNI will be stripped.

jordan_support: Repro steps from customer:
1) From a workstation behind corp proxy: `curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 https://private-redwood.example.corp/v1/engines/gpt-4/infer`
2) They get `curl: (56) Received HTTP/0.9 when not allowed` or `SSL: TLSV1_ALERT_UNKNOWN_CA` depending on client.

maria_support: They also sent a packet capture showing the proxy returning `HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established` then injecting `X-Forwarded-Host` and a `Via` header before passing bytes.

samir_neteng: That header injection suggests the proxy is doing an explicit man-in-the-middle or at least poking into the CONNECT body. Key point: an HTTP CONNECT tunnel must forward bytes without changing the TLS ClientHello. If the proxy rewrites bytes or terminates TLS, our server sees either missing SNI or a certificate mismatch.

alice_oncall: Can we find matching errors in our logs for the customer's request time? I.e., `upstream_tls_handshake: failed: sni-empty` or `handshake: unexpected message`?

jordan_support: Pasted snippet from customer request id 01GZ: `upstream_tls_handshake: client_hello_missing_sni` and `connection: closed by peer`.

samir_neteng: Ask them to run these quick checks and send output: 
- `curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 https://private-redwood.example.corp/ -I`
- `openssl s_client -connect private-redwood.example.corp:443 -servername private-redwood.example.corp` (from a host WITH and WITHOUT proxy)
- show proxy config (squid/bluecoat/version) and any `request_header_add` / `reply_header_add` rules.

jordan_support: Customer ran curl and `openssl` via the proxy. Results: `openssl` when going direct works. When going through proxy the `s_client` shows no SNI and the server sent `no cert chosen` alert.

maria_support: Workaround idea: if the proxy supports `CONNECT` to an IP:port target (bypassing host header rewrite) they can add a rule to allow direct TCP for the subnets hosting Redwoods' VPC endpoints. Also adding `no_proxy` for hosts matching `*.private-redwood.example.corp` on client side works.

samir_neteng: Longer term recommendation for customers: require the enterprise proxy to preserve raw CONNECT tunnels for TLS on port 443 and not inspect/alter the ClientHello. If inspection is required (DPI with TLS interception), they must install the enterprise CA into clients AND ensure the proxy forwards the original SNI in a header we can opt into for legacy setups — but note that terminating proxies break end-to-end TLS and are incompatible with client certificate verification.

alice_oncall: For our Private deployments we can detect `client_hello_missing_sni` and map to a clearer support message. We should also add a KB article describing: allowed proxy behaviors, how to test, and curl/openssl repros.

jordan_support: Customer patch: they allowed `CONNECT` passthrough for the FQDNs and disabled header rewrite for the matching route. After change they reported success: `200 OK` and inference calls completed.

maria_support: They also added `no_proxy` for the SDK container used by their app as temporary mitigation.

samir_neteng: For follow-up, ask networking team at the customer to: 
- whitelist destination IPs/hostnames in their egress allowlist (so proxy won't intercept)
- allow raw TCP CONNECT to port 443 to the Redwood endpoint (no TLS termination)
- if they must terminate TLS, add our signing cert to their trust store and coordinate cert pinning decisions.

jordan_support: Filing internal follow-up ticket to add a KB and update our Private onboarding checklist to include: proxy tests, sample `curl` commands, and common error messages.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-4821 for KB + onboarding change.

alice_oncall: Nice. I'll draft the KB and include examples and packet capture indicators (missing SNI, `HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established` followed by altered bytes).

jordan_support: Customer confirmed all good and will close the support case after we push the KB link. :thumbsup:
